value: Grok 'cf-framework-benchmark optimization research' (May 2026) is mostly invalid for this repo: (1) Audit-enforced controls already cover its top items - cloudflare:optimization-audit shows 0 risk classes across 18 frameworks (no broad-prefetch, no chart/media hydration-on-entry, no boundary leaks). cloudflare:config-audit passes with 0 gaps. (2) Runner methodology claims (PerformanceObserver for LCP/INP, newContext per iteration, cfWorker server-timing, 103 Early Hints CDP capture, cf-ray/colo) are ALREADY implemented in bench/src/run.mjs - it uses web-vitals.js (which IS PerformanceObserver under the hood) and parses server-timing by name into serverTimingSummary. (3) Contract-violating recommendations (NDJSON streaming /api/prices, Durable Object WebSockets for /chart, AI Gateway prefix caching for non-AI routes, Cache Rules dashboard config) bypass the v5 contract or change workload. (4) chart-core compute is INTENTIONAL stress workload - memoizing indicators is a fairness violation. (5) Hallucinations: claims that React Router lacks v8_splitRouteModules (already true), that media apps need fetchpriority='high' on hero images (current low/lazy thumbnails are correct - they aren't LCP candidates), that OpenNext GC fix is repo-actionable (it's upstream). Verdict: no silent same-contract changes warranted; recommendations either already done, contract-violating, or upstream. Conservative path: any compatibility_date bump must be a deliberate platform-era-disclosure update with re-bench, not a silent edit.

Second-round 'decision-grade' optimization research (May 6, 2026) for cf-framework-benchmark: same verdict as first round — NO-OP. Per-item: (1) Remove nodejs_als/global_fetch_strictly_public from apps/next: INVALID — OpenNext requires ALS for RSC/middleware context propagation; cloudflare-best-practices.md explicitly says compat flags are benchmark metadata, NOT optimization knobs. (2) Same flag on apps/waku: required for Waku alpha context. (3) Astro waitUntil onRequest hook: INVALID — current astro.config.mjs is minimal; adding out-of-band work changes request lifecycle, not in v5 contract, bucket-changing. (4) Nuxt nitro.prerender.autoSubfolderIndex:false: N/A — Nuxt entry uses cloudflare_module runtime SSR, not prerendering benchmark routes. (5) Vue Lazy Hydration / Suspense: bucket-changing (alters declared hydrationModel). (6) Canvas Uint32Array micro-opt for /chart: INVALID — chart-core is intentional stress workload (line 4 comment). (7) Playwright isLocal:true CDP flag: N/A — runner uses chromium.launch, not connectOverCDP. (8) Durable Object queue+WebSocket for /chart: contract-violating (changes /api/prices from HTTP fetch to WS, alters API contract). (9) Smart Placement: already tracked as smart-placement-entry-worker variant (optimized-only, requires-bindings). (10) Hono TrieRouter swap: diagnostic-only at most; RegExpRouter is generally faster, no fairness benefit. (11) OpenNext R2 regional cache / enableCacheInterception: already tracked as opennext-r2-regional-cache and opennext-cache-mode variants. (12) Playwright sharding: methodology choice, not fairness improvement; current sequential newContext-per-iteration is by design for measurement isolation. Verdict: identical to first-round Grok report — recommendations are already-tracked as optimized-only variants, adapter-required (policy forbids silent normalization), contract-violating, workload-violating, or N/A. No same-contract changes warranted.
